text: dsh-plain-approvals 是一款面向 DSH 的审批与提问文案插件，会把操作审批说明改写成中文和英文的易读提示，并按读取、写入、删除或其他类别组织文案、展示可识别的文件路径。它在审批请求到达界面前处理展示文字，也会收集工具调用摘要以辅助说明操作类别；遇到非中文问题时，可调用当前模型改写问题、标题和选项描述，同时保留选项标签。适合希望更容易理解 DSH 审批卡片和模型问题的用户。问题改写使用当前 DSH 模型服务；插件不要求单独配置 API 密钥。

dsh-plain-approvals makes DSH approval cards and model questions easier to understand. It formats approvals by operation type and shows detected paths. For non-Chinese questions, it uses the current model to rewrite text while preserving option labels. No separate API key is configured.
想让 DSH 的审批提示少一点术语，多一点人话。
批准文件操作前，能不能先看懂它会读写哪些路径？
希望危险操作和普通写入在审批卡片上有不同提示。
把 DSH 弹出的英文问题改成普通中文，但选项值不要变。
让审批说明把命令里能识别的文件路径列出来。
遇到套了 bash 或 PowerShell 的命令时，也想看到里面操作的大致类别。
Can approval prompts explain whether a tool call reads, writes, or deletes files?
I want clearer Chinese wording for model questions without changing the answer choices.
Can an approval card show file paths detected in a shell command?
dsh-plain-approvals 的功能「审批说明改写」：把审批展示文字组织成中英文提示，并按读取、写入、删除或其他操作类别呈现。收到审批请求时自动处理；可用时会补充工具参数或命令中提取的文件路径。
dsh-plain-approvals 的功能「问题通俗改写」：将非中文的模型问题、标题和选项描述改写成通俗中文。收到问题请求时自动调用当前模型，跳过已是中文的问题，并保留选项标签和问题标识。
dsh-plain-approvals 的功能「命令操作说明」：对常见 shell、PowerShell、Python 等包装命令中的嵌套脚本进行有限层级展开，并据可识别内容补充操作类别和路径提示。
dsh-plain-approvals 的功能「诊断日志」：记录插件激活及审批、问题改写的处理结果，写入用户主目录下的日志文件；日志采用异步写入并有队列及文件大小上限。
dsh-plain-approvals 使用 DSH 当前模型服务改写非中文问题；是否发送文本以及处理方式取决于所配置的模型提供方。

dsh-plain-approvals README · dsh-plain-approvals：[中文](README.zh.md) | English

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) profile plugin that rewrites the two most technical moments of the UI into plain language:

- **Approval cards** — risk-classified, with the exact files an operation will touch;
- **Model questions** — rewritten into plain language by the current model, with stable answer vocabulary preserved.

Everything is fail-open: if rewriting fails for any reason, the original text is shown and the operation is never blocked or altered.

dsh-plain-approvals README · dsh-plain-approvals：> **Status: tested against DSH `0.2.1-rc.3`.** This plugin hooks *internal* seams (Cordis waterfalls and the browser panel's `displayReason` field). Those are not public API and may change in future DSH releases. When they do, the plugin degrades to showing the original text.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Install：> **The profile matters.** The desktop client loads the `desktop` profile. Installing into `web` (or any other name) leaves the desktop build unable to see the plugin — the most common "installed but nothing happens" case.

dsh-plain-approvals README · One-click install (recommended)：- **Windows**: double-click `install.bat` in this folder.
- **macOS / Linux**: run `node install.mjs` in this folder.

The script finds Node itself (PATH, the usual install dirs, and DSH's bundled runtime), finds the DSH CLI itself, and installs into `desktop` by default; it then prints the next step (restart DSH).
No environment variables to configure first, spaces and non-ASCII directories in the path are fine, and `package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` are backed up before anything changes.
dsh-plain-approvals README · One-click install (recommended)：Pick another profile with `install.bat --profile <name>` or `node install.mjs --profile <name>`.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Manual install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:MMMichelsa/dsh-plain-approvals
```

Pinned version (recommended once the tag exists):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:MMMichelsa/dsh-plain-approvals#v1.1.1
```

dsh-plain-approvals README · Manual install：> Not on the desktop build (CLI/TUI)? Replace `desktop` with your own profile name. Installation needs network access: pnpm fetches the repository from GitHub.
>
> If `git` is not installed (pnpm reports a git error), install from the tarball instead:
>
> ```powershell
> dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://codeload.github.com/MMMichelsa/dsh-plain-approvals/tar.gz/refs/heads/main
> ```

dsh-plain-approvals README · Manual install：Confirm `dsh-plain-approvals` ends up in the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`.
Uninstall with `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plain-approvals` and remove it from `dsh.profile.bundles`.

Local development (link a checkout):

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<absolute path to this repo>
```

dsh-plain-approvals README · What it looks like：```text
Before: Allow this operation with danger-full-access permissions: update the profile config

After:  ⚠️ 会写入文件，请确认。助手要把「write」这一次调用放宽到 danger-full-access 权限
        （沙箱几乎完全关闭：可以读写这台电脑上的任意文件、运行任意系统命令、访问网络），

Delete / overwrite operations get a louder 🔴 card with the exact paths they will remove or overwrite.

dsh-plain-approvals README · What it looks like：Commands that wrap another script are unwrapped too: `bash -c "rm -rf x"`, `sh -c …`, `python -c …`,
`cmd /c …`, `pwsh -Command …`, and even `powershell -EncodedCommand <base64>` is decoded and read.
Up to three levels deep; when the budget runs out the card says so instead of pretending it saw
everything — and a deeply nested command can never hang the host.
English cards carry the same information, e.g. `🔴 DESTRUCTIVE OPERATION — please confirm. The agent wants to widen this one "pwsh" call to danger-full-access (…), and it will delete or overwrite: …`.

dsh-plain-approvals README · What it looks like：```text
Before: Which sandbox mode should the retry use?  (option labels: workspace-write / danger-full-access)

After: 这次重试应该用哪种权限？ (option labels unchanged; descriptions gain the Chinese explanation)
```

dsh-plain-approvals README · What it changes：| UI | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Read-type approval (rare) | `Allow this operation with read-only permissions: …` | `🟢 读取操作：这次只是读取 <path>，不会改动任何文件。…` |
| Write-type approval | `Allow this operation with danger-full-access permissions: …` | `⚠️ 会写入文件，请确认。…并会写入：<path list>。…` |
| Delete / overwrite approval | same | `🔴 高危操作，请确认！…它会删除或覆盖：<path list>。…` |
| Command approval without an obvious delete/overwrite | technical wording | `⚙️ 需要你批准：…没有发现明显的删除或覆盖指令，但命令仍可能有副作用…` |
| Other approvals | the asker's own wording | `【需要你批准】…` |
| Model question cards | model wording (possibly English or jargon) | rewritten into plain Chinese; **option labels stay byte-identical**, descriptions gain a label explanation |

dsh-plain-approvals README · Risk classification：| Class | Basis | Presentation |
|---|---|---|
| Read | tool name is `read`, `read_image`, `glob`, `grep`, `web_fetch`, … | `🟢` read-only note, never a high-risk warning |
| Write | `write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` / `str_replace_editor`; or a command whose first word is `Set-Content`, `Add-Content`, `Out-File`, `Copy-Item`, `Move-Item`, `New-Item`, `tee`, …; or a `> file` output redirect | `⚠️ 会写入文件` plus the paths |
| Delete | `delete_file` / `remove_file`, …; or a command whose first word is `rm`, `del`, `rd`, `ri`, `rmdir`, `Remove-Item`, `Clear-Content`, …; or `git clean` / `git reset --hard` / `git checkout --`; or `shutil.rmtree` / `os.remove` inside a script | `🔴 高危操作` plus the paths |
| Other | shell commands without any of the above; unknown tools | neutral `⚙️` note |

dsh-plain-approvals README · Risk classification：Approval requests do not carry tool arguments (by design in DSH), so the plugin caches each call's `arguments` from `tools/pre-execute` (keyed by `callId`, cleared on `tools/result`, at most 256 entries). File paths for `write` / `edit` come from `file_path` exactly; for `pwsh` / `bash` they are extracted heuristically from the command and the card says so. When neither source yields a path, the plugin falls back to paths found in the approval note, and otherwise says the path is unknown instead of guessing.

dsh-plain-approvals README · How it works：- `approval/request` and `user-questions/request` are Cordis waterfalls that the host forwards to the browser panel. The plugin registers with `ctx.on(event, listener, { prepend: true, global: true })`, gets the same request object first, and:
  - approvals: replaces `displayReason` (`{ en, zh }`, presentation only);
  - questions: calls the current model provider to rewrite `question / header / option.description`.
- Tool arguments are `deepFreeze`d by `dsh-tools`, so question objects are read-only. The plugin clones them, rewrites the clones, and replaces `request.questions`; approval request objects are writable, so `displayReason` is replaced in place.
- Question rewriting only runs when some displayed text is not Chinese; fully Chinese questions are skipped at zero cost.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Cost：- Approvals: local templates, **zero tokens, zero latency**.
- Questions: one small model call per batch (about 1–3 s, a few hundred tokens), 15 s timeout; skipped entirely for Chinese-only questions. Results are cached in memory (up to 64 cards), so identical questions never cost twice.
- Fail-open everywhere: missing model, timeout, invalid output, label mismatch → original text.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Copy and localization：All user-visible copy lives in [`locale/zh.json`](locale/zh.json) and [`locale/en.json`](locale/en.json); the code only fills placeholders. A missing key falls back to English, and a key missing from both locales drops the sentence rather than printing `{placeholder}`. Change the wording by editing those JSON files — no model call, no code change. The two locale files must have identical keys, which the test suite enforces. Copy is neutral (“the agent” / 「助手」) and carries no author-specific persona.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Diagnostics：The plugin appends one line per event to `~/.dsh/dsh-plain-approvals.log`: activation (with build marker), approval classification (`kind`, sandbox mode, number of paths), question rewrite outcome and failure reason. It never logs command text, approval justifications, or question text. Delete the file at any time; it is recreated.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Privacy and security：- The plugin never approves or denies anything on its own; it only changes display text.
- Question text is sent to the *current* model provider for rewriting — the same provider that produced it. Nothing is sent anywhere else.
- No network calls of its own; no credentials are read.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Development：```bash
npm test            # runs node test/index.test.mjs
```

`node --test` cannot spawn child processes inside DSH's sandbox, so the suite is a plain script using `node:test` directly.
Release steps are in [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md).

dsh-plain-approvals README · Compatibility：- Node.js >= 20.
- Tested on DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` (desktop profile, web UI).
- Relies on internal seams: `approval/request`, `user-questions/request`, `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/result`, and the client approval panel's `displayReason`. Not official API.

dsh-plain-approvals README · Known limitations：- Text-only cards: colors and font sizes are owned by the built-in approval panel; a true red banner needs a separate client-UI plugin.
- Command risk detection is heuristic: short aliases are only matched as the first word of each command segment (so `Get-ChildItem C:\rd\x` is not mistaken for `rd`), while long forms (`Remove-Item`, `shutil.rmtree`) match anywhere in the command. Deletes hidden in encoded or nested scripts can still be missed.
- Shell path extraction is heuristic; it is labeled as such on the card.
- `read` tools do not normally trigger approvals, so the green note is rarely seen in practice.
